description: File a GitHub issue on the repository in `cwd`, through the `gh` CLI (its login, or GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN). PREVIEWS BY DEFAULT: without `dry_run: false` nothing is created, and the tool returns the target repository, the title, labels and assignees it would send, the body's length (the body is sent exactly as given), and what the secrets scan found, and a `previewId`. Show the user that preview with the body you passed; only once they agree, call again with the same arguments plus `dry_run: false` and that `preview_id` (a create without it, with changed arguments, or more than an hour later, is refused; one preview allows one create). If a create returns `create_uncertain`, the issue may exist: check before calling again. Target: the `origin` remote's repository, or its fork parent when issues are disabled (or the repository archived) on `origin`; an explicit `repo` must be one of those two. Title and body are scanned for secrets first: a known secret pattern (high or medium severity) refuses the issue, even with `dry_run: false`; a high-entropy string only warns. Labels should exist on the target repository (GitHub creates a missing one only for someone who can push there).

assignees.description: GitHub logins to assign (`@me` for the signed-in user).

body.description: Issue body, Markdown, sent verbatim (at most 65,536 characters).

cwd.description: Working directory (repo root). Defaults to server cwd.

dry_run.description: Default: true — preview only. Pass false to create the issue, after the user has seen the preview.

labels.description: Label names; each must already exist on the target repository.

preview_id.description: Required with dry_run: false: the `previewId` of a preview of this very issue (same title, body, labels, assignees and target).

repo.description: `owner/repo` to file on: the origin repository or its fork parent. Defaults to origin, or the parent when origin takes no issues.

name: gitwand_create_issue
